key_insight: A confidence-aware LLM system, DIAGNO, matched or outperformed neurologists on neuropathology-grounded differential diagnosis in complex cases.
clinical_relevance: This work suggests AI may help support high-stakes diagnostic reasoning when benchmarked against biological ground truth rather than clinician consensus.
method: Built NeuroBench with 791 retrospective neurological cases tied to autopsy-confirmed diagnoses from three health systems.
Compared DIAGNO top-3 differentials to neurologists in a blinded subset of 203 complex MGH cases.
Used retrieval-augmented generation for lower-confidence cases and independent adjudication against neuropathological ground truth.
evidence_signal: Across validation sets, DIAGNO reached 83.8% top-3 accuracy at MGH, 76.5% at Mount Sinai, and 92.3% at UTHSA; in the adjudicated MGH subset it slightly outperformed neurologists overall.
watch_item: Results come from retrospective, curated cases and may not generalize to real-time bedside use, especially outside expert centers or for less complex presentations.
paper_title: Assessing AI and Neurologist Diagnostic Reasoning Against Neuropathological Ground Truth
